overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance shows that space and planetary 'what-if' scenarios, extreme celestial weather, and existential cosmic scale comparisons dominate engagement velocity. Videos utilizing high-stakes hypothetical survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme physical oddities ('Liquid Diamond Planet', 'Planet of Burning Ice') generate significantly higher views-per-day and like-to-view ratios than standard informational facts or psychological tricks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved over 970-1000+ views with exceptional like ratios (38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical extreme survival scenarios involving bizarre, newly discovered cosmic or geological locations.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible or extreme conditions ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') outperformed standard space facts, securing 700-980 views rapidly.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on counter-intuitive planetary physics and exotic weather phenomena outside of our solar system.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal psychological tricks ('The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head') or memory glitches hovered at lower velocities (50-70 views, minimal engagement).
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychology micro-tips unless paired with a high-stakes visual mystery or cinematic narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: Ancient history mysteries ('The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve') generated modest views (~139) with zero likes or comments, indicating poor initial feed traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid dry historical trivia; if exploring history, pivot to high-concept archaeological mysteries or cinematic survival storytelling.
